newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soyoil ends up on commercial buying, meal up.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soyoil ends up on commercial buying, meal up.

text.p: CBOT soyoil futures ended sharply higher Tuesday on heavy buying by commercial firms and soymeal also ended up on export talk, traders said.
Cargill bought 600 lots May soyoil and 300 July, and ADM bought 300 lots July and 500 lots of May, pit sources said.
Strength from talk that China was buying in South American vegetable oil markets also helped lift prices, traders said.
U.S. export sources said China recently bought from 5,000 to 10,000 tonnes of South American soyoil for shipment during May and June at prices near $500.00 per tonne.
Rumors of business in U.S. soymeal export markets also helped to push those prices higher, traders said.
There was talk that up to 100,000 tonnes of U.S. soymeal was enroute to buyers in western Europe, although no U.S. exporters were able to confirm the business.
Soyoil futures settled up 0.27 to 0.35 cent per lb, with May up 0.30 cent at 24.15 cents, and July ended up 0.33 at 24.59 cents.
CBOT soymeal closed up $0.10 to $3.70 per ton, with May up $2.80 at $277.20 and July up $3.70 at $273.40.
In soymeal trading, Cargill bought 200 lots May and 100 lots July and ADM bought 300 lots May. Smith Barney sold 100 lots May and 100 July, pit sources said.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 16,000 lots, slightly below Monday's actual volume of 16,822 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 20,000 lots, against Monday's final volume of 33,162.
